query: For a multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy exposed to simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature, what single mechanistic hypothesis could explain the accelerated coupled degradation and why it occurs? Specify a controlled comparison capable of distinguishing the proposed explanation, predict the changes in total degradation and the individual wear and corrosion responses relative to a matched baseline, define the relevant boundary conditions, identify supporting evidence, and give a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: In a multi‐phase eutectic high‐entropy alloy, the removal of the protective passive film by mechanical wear under elevated temperature promotes localized corrosion at exposed intermetallic interfaces, which in turn accelerates the overall degradation rate via a synergistic tribocorrosion mechanism.
generation.material_initial_state: A multi‐phase eutectic high‐entropy alloy with a stable passive film protecting its intermetallic phases under benign conditions.
generation.intervention: Subject the alloy to simultaneous controlled sliding wear and exposure to a corrosive electrolyte at an elevated temperature; compare with tests where wear and corrosion are applied separately.
generation.conditions: Elevated temperature relevant to service conditions; a defined corrosive environment (e.g., an oxidizing electrolyte concentration); controlled sliding wear with specified load, speed, and sliding distance to simulate practical wear conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: Disruption of the passive film at intermetallic phase boundaries due to mechanical abrasion, leading to exposed reactive surfaces.
generation.mechanism: Mechanical wear accelerates the removal of the protective passive layer, exposing fresh alloy surfaces that are vulnerable to corrosion. The localized corrosion further degrades these areas, enhancing wear by increasing material roughness and brittleness. This cyclic interaction leads to an accelerated overall degradation compared to when wear or corrosion act in isolation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Total degradation will be significantly accelerated relative to each isolated degradation mode. Specifically, the wear rate is expected to increase due to poor surface protection and altered mechanical properties, while the corrosion rate is also expected to rise due to the continual removal of the passive film.
generation.baseline: Degradation responses (total material loss, wear, and corrosion rates) observed under isolated conditions of wear only or corrosion only.
generation.boundary: Valid under conditions where the alloy initially forms a stable passive film and where both the applied wear and corrosion conditions are within the operational regime assumed by service conditions. Extreme conditions outside these parameters might invoke different mechanisms.
generation.uncertainty: The exact quantitative enhancement in degradation rates for the coupled system versus isolated conditions is uncertain and will require experimental validation; moreover, the relative contributions of wear and corrosion to the synergistic effect might vary with parameter changes.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare specimens of the eutectic high-entropy alloy and conduct three sets of experiments: one under isolated wear conditions, another under isolated corrosion conditions, and a third under simultaneous wear-corrosion conditions at the same elevated temperature. Ensure all other environmental parameters (load, sliding speed, electrolyte composition) are identical between tests.
measurements: Total material loss (mass or volume loss)
Wear track geometry and roughness analysis
Corrosion penetration depth via microscopy or spectroscopy
Surface chemical analysis to monitor the integrity of passive films
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the simultaneous wear-corrosion experiment does not show a statistically significant increase in both wear-induced disruption of the passive film and accelerated corrosion (i.e., overall degradation rate) relative to the isolated wear or corrosion tests, then the proposed synergistic tribocorrosion mechanism is falsified.
